findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 58 mm is observed in the body of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with both the superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein, suggesting potential invasion. No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum is observed. Contact of more than 180° with the splenic artery is also noted, indicating possible invasion. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastasis is observed in one node at station 14t. No other metastases are observed.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU0 (no invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV0 (no invasion of the portal vein)
A1 (contact of more than 180° with the splenic artery, indicating possible invasion)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (contact of more than 180° with both the superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein, suggesting potential invasion)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the local invasion factors identified, the T classification is T3, as there is serosal invasion (S1) and contact of more than 180° with both the superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein (OO1), indicating potential invasion.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the body of the pancreas are:
- Station 14t (left gastric artery lymph nodes)
- Station 15 (common hepatic artery lymph nodes)
- Station 16 (proper hepatic artery lymph nodes)
- Station 17 (gastroduodenal artery lymph nodes)
- Station 18 (common bile duct lymph nodes)
- Station 19 (cystic duct lymph nodes)
- Station 13 (splenic artery lymph nodes)

The patient's metastatic lymph node station is 14t, which is regional. There is only one metastatic lymph node at station 14t. Therefore, the N classification is N1a.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

There are no distant metastases observed, only a single lymph node metastasis at station 14t. Therefore, the M classification is M0.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the resectability classification is Resectable (R), as there are no criteria for Borderline Resectable (BR) or Unresectable (UR) met.

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the determined T (T3), N (N1a), and M (M0) categories, the overall stage is Stage IIA.
